text: EX-99.1 2 d160614dex991.htm EX-99.1 EX-99.1 Exhibit 99.1 Dana Incorporated Reports Strong Third-Quarter Results; Eaton Mobility Transaction on Track; Increases Share Repurchases Third-Quarter Highlights: • Sales of $2.0 billion, an increase of $121 million versus the third quarter of 2025 • Net income of $15 million, including $29 million from discontinued operations and $41 million of debt-extinguishment and net tax charges • Adjusted EBITDA of $218 million; $56 million higher than third quarter of 2025 • 10.7 percent adjusted EBITDA margin; 220 basis points higher than prior year • Achieved $60 million in cost savings year to date • Repurchased 6.6 million shares, returning $200 million to shareholders • Year-to-date shareholder repurchases of $369 million • Planning an additional ~$100 million of repurchases in the fourth quarter of 2026 • Eaton Mobility transaction remains on track to close around the end of the first quarter of 2027 • Nearly all regulatory approvals have been obtained with only one pending MAUMEE, Ohio, October 28, 2026 – Dana Incorporated (NYSE: DAN) today announced its third-quarter 2026 financial results, delivering strong performance with higher sales and expanding margins. “Dana delivered strong third-quarter results, reflecting our continued focus on operating the business well and executing our strategy with discipline,” said Byron Foster, Chief Executive Officer. “Productivity gains, commercial initiatives, and structural cost reductions are driving meaningful margin improvement as we capitalize on stronger commercial vehicle demand and continue to return capital to shareholders. As we work toward closing the Eaton Mobility transaction, we remain firmly focused on delivering strong performance today while preparing to create an even stronger, more diversified company positioned for long-term growth and shareholder value.” Sales in the third quarter of 2026 totaled $2.04 billion, compared with $1.92 billion in the same period of 2025. The increase was primarily driven by stronger commercial vehicle demand, backlog conversion, and commercial and cost-recovery actions. Adjusted EBITDA for the third quarter was $218 million, representing a 10.7 percent margin, compared with $162 million, 8.5 percent margin, for the same period in 2025. Cost-savings actions, operational efficiency improvements, and commercial initiatives were the primary drivers of the improvement. Net loss from continuing operations was $10 million in the third quarter of 2026, compared with net income of $13 million in the same period of 2025. Diluted loss per share from continuing operations was $0.13, compared with diluted earnings per share of $0.07 last year. Significantly improved operating performance and lower net interest expense were more than offset by a $24 million loss on the extinguishment of debt and higher income tax expense, including a $29 million charge related to the settlement of a foreign income tax partially offset by a $12 million benefit associated with post Off-Highway sale restructuring actions. Adjusted net income improved to $44 million in the third quarter of 2026 from an adjusted net loss of $5 million in the prior-year period, while diluted adjusted earnings per share improved to $0.41 from an adjusted loss per share of $0.04. Operating cash flow was $102 million in the third quarter of 2026, compared with $111 million in the prior-year period. Adjusted free cash flow was $66 million, compared with $101 million in the prior-year period. Higher earnings from continuing operations and lower one-time costs, net interest and cash taxes partially offset the absence of cash generation from the divested Off-Highway business, higher capital spending, and working capital timing. 1 Dana today announced an increase in its planned share repurchases ahead of the closing of the Eaton Mobility transaction. During the third quarter, the company repurchased approximately 6.6 million shares for $200 million, bringing year-to-date capital returned to shareholders through share repurchases to $369 million. Dana expects to repurchase an additional $100 million of shares in the fourth quarter of 2026. “We continue to see compelling strategic and financial benefits from the combination with Eaton Mobility and are confident in the value the transaction will create for our shareholders, customers, and employees,” Foster added. “As we move toward closing, we are also maximizing the opportunities available to return capital to shareholders. Our increased fourth-quarter repurchases underscore our confidence in Dana and our commitment to shareholder value.” Dana has revised its full-year guidance, raising its sales outlook by approximately $50 million, reflecting higher demand and recoveries. The company maintained its adjusted EBITDA, diluted adjusted EPS, and adjusted free cash flow guidance. Note Regarding Use of Non-GAAP Financial Measures In addition to the financial measures presented in accordance with U.S. generally accepted accounting principles (“U.S. GAAP”), this communication includes certain non-GAAP financial measures (collectively, the “Non-GAAP Measures”), such as adjusted EBITDA, adjusted EBITDA margin, adjusted net income (loss) attributable to the parent company, diluted adjusted EPS, and adjusted free cash flow. Adjusted EBITDA is a non-GAAP financial measure which we have defined as net income (loss) before interest, income taxes, depreciation, amortization, equity grant expense, restructuring expense, expenses related to the acquisition of the Eaton Mobility business, non-service cost components of pension and other postretirement benefit costs and other adjustments not related to our core operations (gain/loss on debt extinguishment, pension settlements, divestitures, impairment, etc.). Adjusted EBITDA is a measure of our ability to maintain and continue to invest in our operations and provide shareholder returns. We use adjusted EBITDA in assessing the effectiveness of our business strategies, evaluating and pricing potential acquisitions and as a factor in making incentive compensation decisions. In addition to its use by management, we also believe adjusted EBITDA is a measure widely used by securities analysts, investors and others to evaluate financial performance of our company relative to other Tier 1 automotive suppliers. Adjusted net income (loss) attributable to the parent company is a non-GAAP financial measure which we have defined as net income (loss) attributable to the parent company, excluding any discrete income tax items, restructuring charges, expenses related to the acquisition of the Eaton Mobility business, amortization expense and other adjustments not related to our core operations (as used in adjusted EBITDA), net of any associated income tax effects. This measure is considered useful for purposes of providing investors, analysts and other interested parties with an indicator of ongoing financial performance that provides enhanced comparability to net income (loss) attributable to the parent company reported by other companies. Adjusted net income (loss) attributable to the parent company is neither intended to represent nor be an alternative measure to net income (loss) attributable to the parent company reported in accordance with GAAP. 4 Diluted adjusted EPS is a non-GAAP financial measure which we have defined as adjusted net income (loss) attributable to the parent company divided by adjusted diluted shares. We define adjusted diluted shares as diluted shares as determined in accordance with GAAP based on adjusted net income (loss) attributable to the parent company. This measure is considered useful for purposes of providing investors, analysts and other interested parties with an indicator of ongoing financial performance that provides enhanced comparability to EPS reported by other companies. Diluted adjusted EPS is neither intended to represent nor be an alternative measure to diluted EPS reported in accordance with GAAP. Adjusted free cash flow is a non-GAAP financial measure which we have defined as net cash provided by (used in) operating activities less purchases of property, plant and equipment plus proceeds from sale of property, plant and equipment plus cash paid for purchase of electric capacity demand rights plus cash paid for Off-Highway business divestiture related activities and cash paid for Eaton Mobility acquisition related activities. We believe adjusted free cash flow is useful to investors in evaluating the operational cash flow of the company inclusive of the spending required to maintain the operations. Adjusted free cash flow is not intended to represent nor be an alternative to the measure of net cash provided by (used in) operating activities reported in accordance with GAAP. Adjusted unlevered free cash flow is also a non-GAAP financial measure, which we have defined as adjusted free cash flow less cash interest, net. These Non-GAAP Measures should not be used in isolation or as a substitute or alternative to results determined in accordance with U.S. GAAP. In addition, Dana’s and Eaton’s definitions of these Non-GAAP Measures may not be comparable to similarly titled non-GAAP financial measures reported by other companies. A reconciliation of these Non-GAAP Measures to the most directly comparable financial measures calculated and reported in accordance with U.S. GAAP can be found in Dana’s filings with the SEC, except for financial guidance, projections and other forward-looking information since such a reconciliation is not practicable without unreasonable effort as Dana is unable to reasonably forecast certain amounts that are necessary for such reconciliation. For example, we have not provided a reconciliation of our adjusted EBITDA outlook to the most comparable GAAP measures of net income (loss). Providing net income (loss) guidance is potentially misleading and not practical given the difficulty of projecting event-driven transactional and other non-core operating items that are included in net income (loss), including restructuring actions, asset impairments and certain income tax adjustments. The accompanying reconciliations of these non-GAAP measures with the most comparable GAAP measures for the historical periods presented are indicative of the reconciliations that will be prepared upon completion of the periods covered by the non-GAAP guidance. About Dana Incorporated Dana Incorporated (NYSE: DAN) is a global leader in the design and manufacture of highly efficient propulsion solutions for the light- and commercial-vehicle markets. Guided by its vision to be the world’s best powertrain company, Dana delivers advanced conventional and clean-energy technologies that help customers improve the performance, efficiency, and durability of their vehicles. The company supplies leading vehicle manufacturers and related aftermarkets with industry-defining drive systems, electrodynamic technologies, and thermal and sealing solutions. Headquartered in Maumee, Ohio, USA, Dana reported sales of $7.5 billion in 2025. With a history dating to 1904, the company employs 27,000 people in 24 countries across six continents. Note Regarding Use of Non-GAAP Financial Measures In addition to the financial measures presented in accordance with U.S. generally accepted accounting principles (“U.S. GAAP”), this communication includes certain non-GAAP financial measures (collectively, the “Non-GAAP Measures”), such as adjusted EBITDA, adjusted EBITDA margin, adjusted net income (loss) attributable to the parent company, diluted adjusted EPS, and adjusted free cash flow. Adjusted EBITDA is a non-GAAP financial measure which we have defined as net income (loss) before interest, income taxes, depreciation, amortization, equity grant expense, restructuring expense, expenses related to the acquisition of the Eaton Mobility business, non-service cost components of pension and other postretirement benefit costs and other adjustments not related to our core operations (gain/loss on debt extinguishment, pension settlements, divestitures, impairment, etc.). Adjusted EBITDA is a measure of our ability to maintain and continue to invest in our operations and provide shareholder returns. We use adjusted EBITDA in assessing the effectiveness of our business strategies, evaluating and pricing potential acquisitions and as a factor in making incentive compensation decisions. In addition to its use by management, we also believe adjusted EBITDA is a measure widely used by securities analysts, investors and others to evaluate financial performance of our company relative to other Tier 1 automotive suppliers. Adjusted net income (loss) attributable to the parent company is a non-GAAP financial measure which we have defined as net income (loss) attributable to the parent company, excluding any discrete income tax items, restructuring charges, expenses related to the acquisition of the Eaton Mobility business, amortization expense and other adjustments not related to our core operations (as used in adjusted EBITDA), net of any associated income tax effects. This measure is considered useful for purposes of providing investors, analysts and other interested parties with an indicator of ongoing financial performance that provides enhanced comparability to net income (loss) attributable to the parent company reported by other companies. Adjusted net income (loss) attributable to the parent company is neither intended to represent nor be an alternative measure to net income (loss) attributable to the parent company reported in accordance with GAAP. Diluted adjusted EPS is a non-GAAP financial measure which we have defined as adjusted net income (loss) attributable to the parent company divided by adjusted diluted shares. We define adjusted diluted shares as diluted shares as determined in accordance with GAAP based on adjusted net income (loss) attributable to the parent company. This measure is considered useful for purposes of providing investors, analysts and other interested parties with an indicator of ongoing financial performance that provides enhanced comparability to EPS reported by other companies. Diluted adjusted EPS is neither intended to represent nor be an alternative measure to diluted EPS reported in accordance with GAAP. Adjusted free cash flow is a non-GAAP financial measure which we have defined as net cash provided by (used in) operating activities less purchases of property, plant and equipment plus proceeds from sale of property, plant and equipment plus cash paid for purchase of electric capacity demand rights plus cash paid for Off-Highway business divestiture related activities and cash paid for Eaton Mobility acquisition related activities. We believe adjusted free cash flow is useful to investors in evaluating the operational cash flow of the company inclusive of the spending required to maintain the operations. Adjusted free cash flow is not intended to represent nor be an alternative to the measure of net cash provided by (used in) operating activities reported in accordance with GAAP. Adjusted unlevered free cash flow is also a non-GAAP financial measure, which we have defined as adjusted free cash flow less cash interest, net. These Non-GAAP Measures should not be used in isolation or as a substitute or alternative to results determined in accordance with U.S. GAAP. In addition, Dana’s and Eaton’s definitions of these Non-GAAP Measures may not be comparable to similarly titled non-GAAP financial measures reported by other companies. A reconciliation of these Non-GAAP Measures to the most directly comparable financial measures calculated and reported in accordance with U.S. GAAP can be found in Dana’s filings with the SEC, except for financial guidance, projections and other forward-looking information since such a reconciliation is not practicable without unreasonable effort as Dana is unable to reasonably forecast certain amounts that are necessary for such reconciliation. For example, we have not provided a reconciliation of our adjusted EBITDA outlook to the most comparable GAAP measures of net income (loss). Providing net income (loss) guidance is potentially misleading and not practical given the difficulty of projecting event-driven transactional and other non-core operating items that are included in net income (loss), including restructuring actions, asset impairments and certain income tax adjustments. The accompanying reconciliations of these non-GAAP measures with the most comparable GAAP measures for the historical periods presented are indicative of the reconciliations that will be prepared upon completion of the periods covered by the non-GAAP guidance.
